:::{#thm-complex-arithmetic}
#### Adding and multiplying complex numbers

For real numbers $a, b, c, d$:

$$(a + b\,i) + (c + d\,i) = (a + c) + (b + d)\,i$$

and

$$(a + b\,i)(c + d\,i) = (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)\,i.$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

**Sum.**

$$
\ba
(a + b\,i) + (c + d\,i)
&= a + c + b\,i + d\,i
&& \text{(rearrange the terms)}
\\
&= (a + c) + (b + d)\,i
&& \text{(factor out } i \text{)}
\ea
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

**Product.**

$$
\ba
(a + b\,i)(c + d\,i)
&= ac + ad\,i + bc\,i + bd\,i^2
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= ac + ad\,i + bc\,i - bd
&& \text{(@def-imaginary-unit)}
\\
&= (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)\,i
&& \text{(group the real terms and the terms with } i \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

::: notes
@axler2024linear [Definition 1.1, p. 2] takes these two formulas as the definitions of addition and multiplication.
:::
